title: Grove requires a maxExchangeRate on vault deposits, capping how much underlying one share may represent
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.7.2.2.4.3 records a protection absent from the earlier integration documentation: "Controllers now have protections that require a `maxExchangeRate` to be set for deposits. The following ensures 1 share can represent at most 2 USDC."

```
setMaxExchangeRate(GROVE_X_STEAKHOUSE_USDC_V2, 1e18, 2e6)
```

The threat it addresses is specific to share-based vaults. When Grove deposits, the number of shares it receives is `assets / exchangeRate`, and the rate is reported by the vault itself. If that rate can be inflated — by a donation to the vault's balance, by a manipulated price oracle in its strategy, or simply by a buggy accounting update — Grove hands over full value and receives too few shares. A conventional minimum-output check on shares does not help, because the relayer computing that minimum would be using the same corrupted rate.

Capping the rate instead makes the check independent of the relayer's arithmetic: whatever the vault claims, Grove will not transact if a share purportedly represents more underlying than governance has sanctioned. This is the same move as bounding a Uniswap swap against a TWAP rather than spot (A...2.1.2.9.1.3) — anchor to a value the counterparty cannot move within the transaction.

The scope is worth noting: the parameter guards **deposits** only. Withdrawals are unaffected, consistent with Grove's general stance that exits are never impeded — and defensible, because an inflated rate on exit works in Grove's favour.
description: setMaxExchangeRate(vault, 1e18, 2e6) means a deposit reverts if the vault reports a share worth more than 2 USDC — a guard against depositing into an inflated share price.
